description: Developing Orbit Health as a solo participant. This project is a real time medical monitoring dashboard designed to track astronaut vitals and provide proactive countermeasure protocols during orbital missions.
summary:
Project Overview & What We Developed

Orbit Health is an autonomous, real-time medical monitoring dashboard built to safeguard astronauts during long-duration spaceflights. By integrating continuous Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) biometric telemetry—from wearable Bioshirt Sensor Arrays and Wristband Motion Packs—with NASA open space science data, it tracks critical health indicators including heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, blood sugar, radiation exposure, circadian sleep cycles, and mood. Through color-coded diagnostics, dynamic trend charts, and encrypted cloud logging, it empowers crews to evaluate and act on their health independently.

 The Real-World Problem & Why We Are Doing This

In space, astronauts face five major hazards: microgravity, space radiation, isolation, confinement, and hostile closed environments. Without Earth’s gravity, bodily fluids shift upward, bones lose roughly 1.5% of their density per month, muscles atrophy, immune systems weaken, and astronauts risk Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), cardiovascular strain, and sleep disruption. Because deep-space missions introduce severe communication delays and prevent emergency returns to Earth, crews cannot rely solely on ground flight surgeons. We built Orbit Health to replace reactive checkups with proactive, automated anomaly detection—giving astronauts immediate guidance to prevent minor physiological shifts from becoming life-threatening emergencies.
details:
Project Overview

Orbit Health is an advanced, autonomous real-time medical monitoring and triage dashboard designed specifically to protect astronauts during long-duration orbital and deep-space missions. It bridges the critical gap in space medicine by shifting protocols from reactive treatments to continuous, proactive physiological preservation.

Why We Chose This Challenge & Why It Matters

Spaceflight exposes astronauts to hostile environments, microgravity, and space radiation, leading to rapid bone density loss, muscle atrophy, fluid shifts, and sleep disruptions. Because deep-space missions face severe communication latency and prevent emergency returns to Earth, astronauts cannot rely solely on ground-based flight surgeons. Orbit Health matters because it provides immediate, onboard diagnostic autonomy, safeguarding crew health and ensuring mission success.

Development Tools & Technologies Used

  • Code Editors & Platforms: Developed using VS Code (Visual Studio Code) for custom coding.
  • Languages & Frameworks: Built with modern HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6), and responsive UI layouts optimized for high-contrast, dark-themed operations.

How It Works & Core Functional Modules

  • Overview: Provides a centralized, bird’s-eye view of all critical crew vitals, health status indicators, and mission telemetry in real-time.
  • Elementary: Manages fundamental baseline health parameters and routine daily checkups for crew members.
  • Triage: Features an adaptive triage logic and color-coded diagnostic engine that instantly categorizes physiological anomalies by severity.
  • Symptom Log: Allows astronauts to manually record subjective symptoms, daily wellness notes, and physiological discomforts.
  • Alerts: Instantly flags health irregularities and triggers automated warnings to bypass communication delays with ground control.
  • Sleep: Continuously tracks circadian rhythms, sleep cycles, and rest quality to combat fatigue in microgravity.
  • Hardware (Vitals Status & Syncing): Connects seamlessly with wearable Bioshirt Sensor Arrays and Wristband Motion Packs via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE).
  • Downlink: Handles secure, checksum-verified data transmission and encrypted cloud logging to sync orbital telemetry safely with ground stations.

Creativity & Innovation Factors

Orbit Health stands out through its fusion of interactive telemetry with intelligent, automated triage, reducing crew cognitive load while maintaining high reliability in low-latency environments.
